request.spec:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A user can watch a person (a toggle on the row, per user; PERSON_WATCHED name=<name>,
PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>); show watched yes/no for the signed-in user. When a watched
person's claim is settled, approved or re-settled, one line NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name>
number=<number> is written per watching user, in the order they started watching, after the
claim's own line and before the rollup lines.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Watching is in: each user can watch or unwatch a person from that person's row, and it notifies on settle, approve and re-settle. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**Stored data:** a new migration `V34__person_watch.sql` adds a `person_watch` table with one row per sheet, person and user. Unwatching deletes the row, so watching again puts that user at the end of the notify order.

**Server:**
- `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/watch?by=<user>` with `{"on": true|false}` starts or stops watching. It writes `PERSON_WATCHED` or `PERSON_UNWATCHED name=<name>`. If the user is already in that state, nothing is written.
- `GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/watches?by=<user>` lists the people the signed-in user watches.
- A new step, `RecordClaimNotify`, sits between the claim's own audit line and the rollup lines in settle, approve and re-settle. When the claim ends up SETTLED, it writes one `NOTIFY user=<watcher> person=<name> number=<number>` line per watcher, oldest watch first. A clerk's settle that leaves the claim PENDING doesn't notify, as the spec expects.
- Bulk settle (`BulkSettleClaims`) also writes the NOTIFY lines.

**Front end:** each person row shows `person-watched` (yes/no for the signed-in user) and a `person-watch` Watch/Unwatch button. A refused watch shows the row's `person-error`.

One choice to check: like every other change in the app, a watch is refused for a viewer. Watching is personal, so you may want viewers to be able to watch; the test doesn't cover it, and it's easy to change.
